newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Skoda sees swing to profit - paper.
newsitem.headline: Czech Skoda sees swing to profit - paper.

text.p: Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s. expects its 1996 gross profit to be close to one billion crowns, after a 166 million crown gross loss in 1995, its general director said in a Czech daily on Monday.
In an interview, Lubomir Soudek also told the economic daily Hospodarske Noviny that he would try to limit foreign investors from taking a significant position in the company.

He said the massive heavy machinery group, based in the western city of Plzen, which makes everything from trucks to tin cans and nuclear components, recorded a 40 billion crown turnover last year after 27 billion in 1995.
He said Skoda's core companies, which exclude joint ventures of the group, reached turnover of 28 billion crowns and exports worth 10 billion.
Company officials were not immediately available to confirm or comment on the figures.
Skoda a.s. is no longer affiliated with the car maker now controlled by Volkswagen AG, Skoda Automobilova a.s..

Soudek, who holds about 25 percent stake in Skoda through a firm he controls, said he was interested in buying more shares in Skoda and limit foreign banks, who have bought up over 10 percent stake, from taking a bigger position.

"Together with the (Czech banks) IPB a.s. and Komercni Banka a.s. we would like control of the company to be done through me and the banks and prevent the entry of more foreign investors, who could limit the firm's development trend in some directions," the paper quoted Soudek as saying.
He added that he has applied to buy an 8.7 percent stake which is still held by the government privatisation agency, the National Property Fund.
Soudek's company NERo s.r.o. bought its stake in Skoda in a government privatisation plan in 1993.

Under Soudek's management, the firm has gone through a large restructuring and expansion process, and now has 43 subsidiaries, a number of joint ventures abroad, and controlling stakes in troubled truck makers Tatra a.s. and Skoda LIAZ a.s..
Some analysts have complained about the firm's lack of transparency in internal financial flows and structure.
